description: This line plot illustrates the training accuracy over time, measured in epochs, for three different parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods: C³A_b=128/2, LoRA_τ=1, and Linear. The x-axis, labeled “Epoch,” spans from 0 to 400 on a linear scale, with tick labels appearing at intervals of 50. The y-axis, labeled “Training Accuracy,” ranges from 0.0 to 1.0 and is also on a linear scale, with major gridlines and tick labels at intervals of 0.2. The plot displays three lines: the C³A_b=128/2 method is represented by a magenta line with circular markers and a solid line style; the LoRA_τ=1 method is shown as a light blue line with circular markers and a solid line style; and the Linear method is depicted as a blue line with circular markers and a solid line style. The C³A_b=128/2 line begins near an accuracy of 0.1 at epoch 0, rises sharply to approximately 0.9 by epoch 50, and then plateaus near 0.95 for the remainder of the epochs. The LoRA_τ=1 line starts near 0.1 at epoch 0, increases steadily to approximately 0.8 by epoch 300, and then exhibits significant fluctuations before dropping to around 0.6 by epoch 400. The Linear line starts near 0.1 at epoch 0, increases steadily to approximately 0.8 by epoch 300, and then remains relatively stable near 0.8 for the remainder of the epochs.
